what: Every kb_search in the R16 re-check returned the warning '(index refresh still running, results may be stale)'. The hits were usable, but the warning stayed on every call.
why: The kb index was still refreshing at the start of the session; no wait or status check was done before searching.
workaround: Used the hits anyway and noted the warning in RECHECK-R16.md.

what: Builder reports that agent-docs/backend/interceptors.agent.md still says getInstance() identifies the instance as 'old values', which contradicts the full interceptors page (N1 in the re-check).
why: Builder's reading of the condensed companion page versus the full page; the chunk shows only snippets, so the contradiction is not confirmed here.

what: kb_get on best-practices/model/initializer-operation.md, section 'Static Initializer Operation for Data Seeding', returned only a keyword line with no procedure text.
why: The section that matched was the :meta chunk (keywords), not the body.
workaround: Recorded as N2 in the re-check; the seeding practice was not read from this page.

what: kb_get with a guessed section name 'Practice' returned '(not found: ...)' for best-practices/backend/external-api-adapter-pattern.md and for best-practices/backend/quartz-scheduled-job.md. The real headings are 'External API Adapter with Factory Provider' and 'Practice > Practice notes: scheduler activator, jobs, own transactions'.
why: The builder guessed the heading. kb_get does not list valid headings when the section is not found.
workaround: Retried with the headingPath copied from kb_search json.

what: kb_get on the meta chunk of best-practices/backend/external-api-adapter-pattern.md returned a keyword line only, not the body. The guidance was found in model-blueprints/external-api-adapter-provider-pattern/backend.md instead.
why: The kb returns the :meta chunk (keywords and summary) for some root sections.
workaround: Read the model-blueprint backend.md section 'Backend guidance > The factory'.

what: kb_get with a path and no section returned an empty stub ('pass section to fetch one', '+11 more sections') for best-practices/backend/AGENTS.md and for agent-docs/backend/authentication-guide.agent.md. The builder had to search again.
why: Path-only kb_get on index or companion files returns no body.
workaround: Searched with kb_search for the authentication page instead.

what: The kb read-discipline guard fired about six times during CLI, build and generator debugging ('3 consecutive searches without consulting the knowledge base', 'Repeated source searching, still no kb consult'). No kb answer existed for most of those questions.
why: The guard counts shell, grep and jar inspection as source searching, including legitimate build debugging.
workaround: Carried on; ran kb_search only for catalog questions.
proposed_target: kb read-discipline guard (kb_guard_pause or exemptions for build output)

what: kb_search for a generated third-actor frontend build failure ('third actor ... duplicate import') returned no relevant hit. The only related page, the dual-actor practice, says three actors work.
why: No catalog page covers the generator duplicate-import failure, so the search had nothing to match.
workaround: Bisected the model with build -f -i runs (see c12-15).

what: agent-docs/backend/platform-behavior-reference.md says the platform has no scheduler and no Quartz component. best-practices/backend/quartz-scheduled-job.md describes starting Quartz through a scheduler activator. The two pages disagree.
why: The Quartz practice describes a Karaf scheduler setup that the platform page says does not exist in the runtime.
workaround: Built an OSGi component with its own executor instead (ReservationJob).

what: The docs do not say what transaction and variable context a plain scheduler thread has. The builder wrote its own transaction handling and cannot use ACTOR in the job.
why: Scheduler threads are outside the request context; the catalog says so only in general terms.
workaround: Job calls a modeled static operation through the dispatcher; no ACTOR is used.

what: Dispatcher.callOperation takes the operation name in the form <asm package>.<Entity>#<operation>. The catalog does not give this form; the builder found it in webshop-asm.model.
why: The catalog shows only the interceptor FQN form, not the callOperation name.
workaround: Used webshop.ShopJobs#releaseExpired taken from the generated ASM model.

what: kb says the checksum file is .generated-files__[actor_fqn] in the module root. The real files in the frontend modules are .generated-files-customer and .generated-files-admin, plus an empty .generated-files.
why: Catalog naming does not match the generated layout.
workaround: Read the real file names with ls before comparing checksums.

what: kb suggests 'mvn clean install -Dignore-checksums' for formatting-only checksum errors. judo.sh build -i sets -DvalidateChecksum=false (judo.sh about line 819). The builder used the judo.sh property; the kb flag was not checked.
why: The catalog flag name does not match what judo.sh passes.
workaround: Ran mvnd with -DvalidateChecksum=false (build still failed for other reasons).

what: A build without -i fails on every generated frontend file ('There are manual changes in the generated files', listing all of src/ in both actors). The build itself reformats generated code with biome after writing, so checksums never match again.
why: build -i leaves the frontend .generated-files empty, and the post-generation format step changes the files; the catalog presents -i only as an option for formatting-only changes.
workaround: Use ./judo.sh build -i for every build from here on.
proposed_target: agent-docs/frontend/README.md (Build fails with checksum mismatch error)

what: Adding a third actor (PaymentGateway, kind SYSTEM, anonymous) makes the generated admin frontend fail biome format: 'Declarations inside of a import declaration may not have duplicates' (for example import type { CsvFile, CsvFile, CsvFileStored, CsvFileStored }). Build reports 120 errors in admin. Removing the actor fixes it; the same error occurs with any third actor, whatever its kind.
why: The judo-ui-react actor template helper (getApiImportsForPage, classDataName) returns each type twice when an operation has both an input and an output, and the admin module has several such operations.
workaround: Deleted the PaymentGateway actor and gave the webhook operation an Admin access instead (see c12-24); admin build passed after that.

what: agent-docs/deployment/local-development.md says build -a updates custom operations for a running backend. In this layout build -a and build -F -KA update ~/.m2 but not application/.karaf/system, which is what ./judo.sh start runs. The app then lacked the new custom operations and interceptor.
why: Start uses the copies in .karaf/system; only a full build refreshes them. Evidence: system jar dated 14:30 without the new classes, m2 jar 14:45 with them.
workaround: Full ./judo.sh build -i before start; the debug interceptor and later fixes were only picked up after that.

what: Every start logs ERROR 'LiquibaseModelDataSourcePrehook: Could not find compatible schema model' (NoClassDefFoundError EolExecutionContext from judo.meta.rdbms.osgi). /system/health stays 503 'Missing platform components: PersistenceReady, InitScriptsCompleted', while the app serves requests.
why: CheckRdbmsModelCompatibility cannot load a class from the epsilon runtime; a platform packaging problem, present since R1 per the builder.
workaround: None; the app runs. Health stays 503.

what: Used the documented route schema_dir=application ./judo.sh schema-upgrade after a pg_dump backup. It finished in 36 s, added the new columns and a stock reservation table, and kept 308 orders. This route failed in R6 and R10 according to GAPS; it worked this round.
why: The catalog now documents the route (schema-evolution.md 'When No Manual Step Is Needed'); the builder confirmed it on the running database.

what: judo query with --select on a reference field (principal, output) fails with 'Subselection required for type ESM_TransferObjectType' (or ESM_Parameter). The CLI does not say which subfields to select.
why: The query tool needs a nested selection for reference fields; the CLI help does not show it.
workaround: Read the value with update --brief or with a plain query of the fields that are scalars.

what: judo query graphql is not available ('Model type graphql is not available').
why: The builder guessed a graphql model type; the CLI has no such type.
workaround: Used judo query esm instead.

what: The CLI schema says realm applies only when an actor is not anonymous, yet the query shows Customer and Admin with anonymous true and realm webshop.
why: Unclear: either the schema text or the stored actors are inconsistent; the chunk does not settle it.
workaround: None recorded.

what: After update ... --add feature --feature releaseReservations --as rowAction, the table action is named releaseReservationsTableOperation. update on ...Table::releaseReservations then fails with 'error element not found', and the builder had to use the longer FQN.
why: A row action is wrapped in a TableOperation with its own name; the CLI does not explain the FQN.
workaround: Used the TableOperation FQN for label and removal.
proposed_target: judo update --as rowAction (FQN of created element)

what: A static operation on an unmapped transfer object cannot be reached by an access: validate fails with 'Access target have to be mapped'. operation.md ends the unmapped section with 'Verify: how an actor reaches the operation was not settled in source'.
why: The catalog leaves the access route open; the validator rule is the only evidence.
workaround: Mapped the transfer object to the one ShopConfig row (no members) and put the static operation on it.

what: The payment webhook is a static operation on the Admin actor (hidden access 'gateway'), called with a bearer token of a technical admin user plus an HMAC signature. An anonymous SYSTEM actor was tried first but made the admin build fail (c12-15).
why: A truly anonymous public endpoint was the catalog's answer, but the third actor broke the build; the Admin route was the least-bad documented option.
workaround: Admin access with DERIVED 0..1 getter ShopConfig!any(); webhook route POST /api/webshop/Admin/PaymentGatewayInfo/receive.

what: best-practices/frontend/dual-actor-frontend-architecture.md says the pattern extends to three or more actors, including an anonymous public actor. In this model a third actor (anonymous SYSTEM) breaks the admin frontend build.
why: The catalog claim is not true for this generator version (see c12-15).
workaround: Removed the third actor from the model.

what: Kb says 'set just those fields on an entity that was not loaded in full' but does not say how to build a payload with identifier and version in custom code.
why: The Pattern 4 text gives the mask and entity idea but not the payload construction.
workaround: Read the generated Product.from and used ProductBuilder.from(Map.of(__identifier, __entityType, __version, stock, soldUnits)).

what: A REST update with a stale __version returns HTTP 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR. The log shows IllegalArgumentException 'Outdated instance to update'. The catalog says the stale check exists but not what status a client gets.
why: The version check throws a plain IllegalArgumentException, which the dispatcher turns into a generic 500.
workaround: Interceptor refuses stale saves with a business error (c12-43).

what: The generated admin UI never sends __version. Two admins edited the same product and the second save overwrote the first silently (stock 11 to 7, audit rows confirm).
why: application/frontend-react/webshop__admin/src/services/data-api/common/utils.ts applyStoredMembers copies __version only if typeof is 'string', but the server sends a number, so it is dropped on load. The catalog says clients must echo __version.
workaround: ProductConflictInterceptor takes the version from the signed identifier when the body has none (c12-43).

what: An i18n label for an enumeration value cannot be set through the extra fragment: the generated key enumerations.PaymentProvider.STUB_FAIL comes later in the same object and wins. The provider options therefore show their model names.
why: Last duplicate key wins in application_default.json; the fragment sits above the generated keys.
workaround: Tests use model names (STUB_FAIL, STUB_SUCCEED); fragment line reverted.

what: The payment provider is an enum on the existing shop settings row (ShopConfig.paymentProvider: STUB_SUCCEED, STUB_FAIL, STUB_TIMEOUT, HTTP). PaymentService picks the adapter from that setting; deployment values come from system properties or environment variables.
why: The catalog gives the adapter pattern but no recipe for a provider an admin can switch at runtime.
workaround: Settings row enum plus PaymentAdapter interface with stub and HTTP adapters.

what: The clock is a parameter, not a global: ReservationService.releaseExpired(LocalDateTime now). The admin button 'Release expired reservations' takes a Minutes input that moves the clock for that run, so the browser test does not sleep.
why: BusinessClock is read once at class load and cannot be changed by a browser test; the catalog has no page for a clock a running app can move.
workaround: Scheduled job passes BusinessClock.now(); tests pass any date.

what: Browser specs failed on helper waits: waitForResponse(/~get$/) timed out on the Shop settings row, and openAddAndApplyFilters hit a strict-mode error because two admin tables each show a Filter button.
why: Test design: the helpers assume one table on screen and a response for every click.
workaround: Waited for rows and used the filter helper per table; screen-based waits instead of response waits.

what: The F72 browser assertion expected one history row 'Status New -> Paid' after the webhook; the count was 0 while the status already read Paid.
why: Not explained in this chunk; the history label or the webhook history path may differ from the screen-based check.
workaround: Test reworked in the next round (not in this chunk).

what: A browser step waited for 'Operation executed successfully' after adding to cart and the message did not show before the timeout.
why: Not explained in this chunk; the add-to-cart success feedback timing or the card lookup likely differs.
workaround: Spec rewritten in the next round.

what: Level9aIntegrationTest did not compile: ShopFault getMessage() returns Optional<String>, and the test called startsWith on it. A second compile error came from calling isStale(Throwable) on a non-static method.
why: Builder misread the generated getter types.
workaround: Used .orElse("") and String.valueOf.

what: 22 integration tests errored with PATTERN_VALIDATION_FAILED on sku: the test data 'L9-25958' does not match the model pattern ^[A-Z]{2}-[0-9]{4}$.
why: Builder's test data ignored the model's sku pattern.
workaround: Changed the test SKU to LN-nnnn; then 22 of 22 pass.

what: A sed -i call without an empty backup suffix failed on macOS ('invalid command code'), so the build script was not edited and a second build started with the old commands.
why: macOS sed needs -i '' ; builder used the GNU form.
workaround: Re-ran sed with -i '' and restarted the script.

what: Payment provider adapter: PaymentAdapter interface with StubPaymentAdapter and HttpPaymentAdapter, PaymentService picks the adapter from the shop setting; provider enum on ShopConfig; failure shown as a readable payment error on the order. Integration and smoke tests passed for the stub decline path.

Payment webhook: static operation PaymentGatewayInfo.receive on the Admin actor with a bearer token; HMAC-SHA256 check of eventId|orderNumber|status; idempotency by event id stored on the order; PAID transition in PaymentService. Unknown order gives 422 UNKNOWN_ORDER.

Stock reservation: checkout creates StockReservation rows for 15 minutes; ReservationJob (OSGi component, own executor) and the admin button 'Release expired reservations' call ShopJobs.releaseExpired through the same service; the admin button takes a minutes input for the clock.

Last-item stock take: StockService.take(product, quantity) writes with the product version and retries once on a stale version when enough stock remains; otherwise the buyer gets NOT_ENOUGH_STOCK. Integration tests (22 Level9a, 35 across order-tests) pass; the parallel two-context browser test was not seen in this chunk.

Fix of review R16-R2: the checkout stock loop in CheckoutCustomImplementation no longer does an unguarded DAO update; it calls StockService.take, so a concurrent loser gets a business refusal instead of a 500.

Two admins, one product: ProductConflictInterceptor (built-in product update) takes the version from the payload or from the signed identifier and refuses a stale save with 422 CONFLICT and a readable message. Checked by REST (second save 422, first 200) and by a browser test (conflict message; repeated change saved). Screenshots in checks/F75.
